newsitem.title: UK: S&P cuts outlook on SEEBOARD to negative.
newsitem.headline: S&P cuts outlook on SEEBOARD to negative.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Wednesday it revised the outlook on the A minus long-term ratings of SEEBOARD Plc and CSW Investments (CSW), the acquisition holding company of SEEBOARD, to negative from stable.
"The outlook revision arises in the course of an ongoing review of the consolidated CSW group and brings the outlook into line with the outlooks on the rest of the group," S&P said in a statement.
S&P said the revised outlook reflects operational pressures on CSW's U.S. operating companies, leading to deterioration of consolidated group creditworthiness.

"Credit deterioration on the part of the CSW group operating companies may limit the potential group support for SEEBOARD (should it ever be required) or heighten the need for cash flow from SEEBOARD elsewhere in the group," the agency said.
SEEBOARD's distribution load is characterized by strong domestic and commercial sectors, and less dependence on large industry than most other RECs, S&P said.

Aggressive cost control efforts should allow SEEBOARD to maintain a stable financial profile, notwithstanding the significant efficiency targets incorporated into its recently tightened distribution price cap.

After its takeover in January 1996 by CSW, the financial profile of the U.K. group (CSW Investments & SEEBOARD) took on very substantial leverage, leading to expectations of modest debt service coverage levels, the agency said.
SEEBOARD's very strong business position and ties to the CSW group have maintained the rating in the low A range.
